title: Emergency Preparedness and Response Plan
purpose: Sets out how the organisation prepares for and responds to potential emergencies — to people and to the environment — including roles, procedures, communication, equipment, testing and review.

questions.text: Which potential emergencies could arise from the work (for example electric shock, fire, spills, injury in a remote place)? Draw on the hazard and aspects registers.
Who does what in an emergency (wardens, first aiders, site contact), and how are they contacted?
At client or mine sites, whose emergency plan applies and how does the organisation fit into it?
How often are responses tested (drills), and how are plans reviewed after a test or a real event?

requiredSections: Communication (internal, emergency services, client or site)
expectedRecords: Records of review after drills and incidents
draftingRules: One procedure per emergency type, written as short numbered steps.
Use only scenarios, roles and contacts the user confirmed; leave placeholders for any not given — never invent phone numbers or names.
Where the work is at a mine or client site, refer to that site's plan rather than replacing it.
reviewerChecklist: Every credible emergency from the registers is covered
Site plans are referenced where they apply

brandingInstructions: Use the organisation's confirmed legal or trading name in the header, its logo reference (describe where the logo goes — do not invent one) and its confirmed brand colours for headings and table header rows. Put the document-control block in the footer or on a cover table. If a branding value is not confirmed, leave a placeholder.
